subject: Nova Health — post-demo: model fit guidance & Redwood eval setup
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@novahealth.ai>, Pete Lang <pete.lang@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Nova Health — post-demo: model fit guidance & Redwood eval setup

Hi Emma / Pete — thanks again for a great demo call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the evals on Redwood.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: deploy an assistant that classifies inbound intake forms and drafts triage summaries for clinical review. High precision on risk labels; sensible, traceable summaries preferred over creative generation.
- Data constraints: ~45k de-identified intake records, variable length (short notes to page-long), must not send PHI to third-party models — must run under Nova's VPC (you mentioned private deployment requirement).
- SLO: P95 latency < 700ms per request for single-record inference once in production; offline batch evals fine to be slower.

Suggested model candidates for evaluation on Redwood (initial shortlist)
- Open models optimized for instruction-following and summarization: Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized), Falcon-40B-instruct (server-side, higher cost), and Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized variant).
- Rationale: Mistral / Llama variants produce concise summaries and are cheaper to run; Falcon is a strong contender if you need higher factuality for edge cases.

What we need from you to run the first round of customer-specific evals (we can do this in Redwood Dedicated or your Private deployment):
1) A 500–1,000 record sample (de-identified) representative of distribution. JSONL preferred (one JSON object per line) with fields: id, prompt_text, gold_label, gold_summary. (I've attached a small sample file: nova_sample_dataset.jsonl)
2) A short seed prompt set / rubric for the summary and label criteria (attached: nova_eval_seed_prompts.csv).
3) Confirmation whether you want automatic ROUGE/BLEU-style metrics for summaries or a human review panel for quality gating on first round.

Proposed scoring criteria (we'll refine with your QA team):
- Labeling: accuracy and F1 on critical risk class (weighted by class importance).
- Summaries: ROUGE-L and a factuality check (model hallucination rate measured against exact entity preservation).
- Human score (optional): 1–5 scale for clinical usefulness and clarity on a stratified sample.

Next steps / timeline
- From Nova: share the sample JSONL + rubric by end of this week (Fri 5/15).
- Redwood: we will provision a sandbox eval runner (no cost, 7-day window) and deliver model comparison report and the evaluation notebook within 5 business days of receiving data.
- Follow-up call to review results and recommended production config: target the week of 5/25.

Attachments: nova_sample_dataset.jsonl (sample schema), nova_eval_seed_prompts.csv (seed prompts + scoring rubrics)

If this looks good I can start provisioning the eval runner and share a secure upload for your sample dataset.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai

From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@novahealth.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Pete Lang <pete.lang@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nova Health — post-demo: model fit guidance & Redwood eval setup

Thanks Dylan — that summary matches our notes. A couple clarifications: 
- We can produce a 750-record sample by EOD Friday. It will be de-identified but will still contain some structured fields (age_range, encounter_type) — hope that’s OK.
- For scoring, we'd prefer: (1) automated metrics for the first pass (ROUGE-L + label F1) and (2) a small human review panel (10% sample) focusing on hallucinations.
- About deployment: initially we want a Dedicated pool, but we need TLS + our KMS integration. Can Redwood run evals against the Dedicated stack (no data leaves region)?

If you can confirm the upload link and that Dedicated evals are available, we'll send the sample.

Best,
Emma Chen
Head of Product, Nova Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@novahealth.ai>, Pete Lang <pete.lang@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-13T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nova Health — post-demo: model fit guidance & Redwood eval setup

Emma — yes to everything. Quick answers: 
- Structured fields are fine. Include them as top-level keys in the JSON objects; our eval harness can filter and stratify by encounter_type.
- We can run the customer-specific evals on Redwood Dedicated in your region with KMS/TLS enabled. Data will stay inside your Dedicated pool; we won't persist any artifacts outside the Dedicated environment unless you ask us to export results.
- Upload: I'll provision a secure S3-compatible endpoint scoped to this eval and share credentials via a separate secured email from our security team. Expect that link within 2 business hours.

I've looped in Marissa to provide an initial recommended model + scoring configuration for the first run (she'll include thresholds to watch for).

-Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@novahealth.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-13T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nova Health — post-demo: model fit guidance & Redwood eval setup

Hi Emma / team — quick note on the evaluation spec we'll run once we have the sample. My recommendations below are conservative to reduce risk of quality regressions during rollout.

1) Models to include (first pass)- Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized q4_0) — baseline for cost/latency- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8) — balanced quality/price- Falcon-40B-instruct (float16) — quality upper bound; include for edge-case analysis

2) Evaluation harness config- Input format: JSONL with fields: id, input_text, encounter_type, gold_label (enum), gold_summary (string). We will map your "prompt_text" field to input_text if present.- Batch size: variable; for Dedicated eval we will run both batch and single-request profiles to simulate offline scoring and live latency.- Metrics: Label F1 (micro & macro), confusion matrix export; Summary ROUGE-L; entity-preservation score (exact-string match on defined entities from your schema); hallucination_count (heuristic).

3) Scoring thresholds to flag regression (we will mark a model as not-ready-for-prod if any of these trip):- Label F1 drop > 3% absolute vs baseline on the 750-sample- ROUGE-L drop > 2.5 points absolute- Hallucination rate > 5% on clinical entities

4) Prompt and decode settings- Seed prompts: we will test both terse and instruction-rich prompt templates included in nova_eval_seed_prompts.csv.- Sampling: greedy / temperature 0.0 for label prediction; temperature 0.2 for summaries with nucleus p=0.9 for diversity testing.

5) Outputs and deliverables- Per-model CSV with per-example predictions and metric columns- Aggregated PDF report with charts + examples of failure modes- An evaluation notebook (Colab) showing how to reproduce the runs on Redwood

If those thresholds look reasonable, we'll proceed. Karthik — if you could prepare the Dedicated sandbox and access plan (KMS scope + upload link) we can start as soon as the sample arrives.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Pete Lang <pete.lang@novahealth.ai>

Date: 2026-05-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nova Health — post-demo: model fit guidance & Redwood eval setup

- Deliver the 750-record JSONL by EOD Friday (5/15).
- Confirm the list of clinical entities we want protected (will add in a separate file called nova_protected_entities.csv).
- Prefer the first-pass to run on Dedicated in us-west-2. Please include cost estimates per model for a 750-record pass.

Looking forward to the report. Please proceed with the sandbox provisioning.

Pete Lang
